scope: Independent read-only review of nofile-owner-next-01 exact three-file delta and existing local final ELF; no production-owner positive execution

findings.assessment: PinFailure starts kNone, is assigned only immediately after the persistent worker pidfd_open or pidfd_getfd fails, and Read requires both result==-EMFILE and one of those exact enum values. Context, metadata, xattr, seal or O_PATH reopen errors cannot select it. The inherited worker itself has no recursive retry.

ReadInheritedAfterAllocationFailure is called synchronously by the original Read caller after persistent completion. Its fixed raw clone call supplies InheritedWorker and the retained local Request; it does not enqueue cloning to the persistent worker. Both call sites use 0x350900, with CLONE_FILES, CLONE_FS and CLONE_SETTLS absent. ReadPinned(true) selects only that copied-table descriptor; the ordinary Worker remains ReadPinned(false) and continues pinning by caller TID.

The second stack has separate mapping/top and clear-tid address, prepared before restricted use. A successful clone is joined with the shared FUTEX_WAIT clear-tid protocol before the local inherited Request can leave scope or its stack can be reused. The completion release/acquire publishes result and context state. Clone failure does not publish output; early worker death without complete becomes EIO. Persistent completion clears its request/command before publishing complete and subsequently accesses only process-lifetime state.

Read holds the existing full Mask and Gate across the inherited clone, metadata, kernel clear-tid and final caller context check. Stop closes admission then waits for Gate, so it cannot retire/reset synchronization during this request. Quiesce remains sticky for the current generation. ResetAfterPrivateFork changes only the private copied state and additionally clears inherited_tid; OwnProcess/Read still reject a different TGID sharing VM. Correct proof of private memory remains an upstream lifecycle requirement.

Nine source blocks were independently located, hashed and found byte-identical: SameContext, ReadContext, startup PIDFD_THREAD namespace authority, Start, Stop, Quiesce, metadata shape/xattr/seals/final inode, final caller-context/ABI/publication/errno, and persistent startup authority. Fallback is reachable only after admitted Start. It does not create namespace authority under NOFILE=0 or treat a name/raw initial stat as provenance. Caller output still publishes only after complete metadata and final checks.

Independently reran the frozen two-worker auditor via objdump on a hash-identical private copy of the existing author host ELF. Two named worker roots, six reachable owner functions and no forbidden libc/TLS/canary/runtime edge passed. Independently read both call-site argument blocks, distinct stack/tid locations, true/false shared-reader modes, trampoline and clear-tid join. The only full-disassembly byte difference is the known input-path header.

material_limits_and_next_evidence.detail: The five kernel-mechanism controls use a smaller worker and the local real-source test rejects UID 0; neither executes this new production path. No such positive result is asserted here.

The exact owner source needs a qualified nonroot/caps-zero/initial-userns Start, then NOFILE=0 and NOFILE=1, preprepared AS=1, real caller table unshare/close/reuse, output atomicity/errno, Stop blocked behind active inherited work, and private fork while a parent request is in flight. The actual Android ELF needs a fresh two-worker closure and both clone call-site review.

Start after already lowering NOFILE to zero still cannot establish its original namespace authority. Virtual O_PATH may still require a new readable FD and fail with EMFILE. These are explicit unsupported cases, not silently bypassed.

This path creates a kernel task and copies the caller table; task/kernel allocation failure remains possible. The inherited worker retains copied descriptor references until kernel task exit; JoinRaw prevents those references escaping past Read return, but this is not a no-resource-allocation metadata path.

Paired ART/native bridge generation transitions, cancellation/last-thread retirement, credentials and namespaces remain separate production gates. Source preservation alone does not prove they run in actual Android.

review_harness_notes: Two local checker assumptions failed and were retained: the ninth fragment began with two comments before the chosen anchor; objdump file-format headers include the copied ELF pathname. Both were resolved by exact fragment SHA and unique known path-header normalization, with no source change. The ELF audit itself returned zero; no ELF execution or positive metadata test was performed.
